correlation.formula: n_eff = 2 / (1 + rho) on binary error indicators

evidence.claim: On 120 scored items spanning six domains, independent scripted vendors yield a joint table with both_wrong=5, a_wrong_b_right=21, a_right_b_wrong=17, both_right=77. Conditional P(codex wrong | claude wrong) = 0.19230769230769232.

Independent pair phi=0.012197843367986655 effective_seats=1.9758983020011198 (near nominal 2). Cloned shared-failure pair phi=0.7986974558201845 effective_seats=1.1119157329813556 (collapses toward 1). Hand 2x2 controls: independent phi=0 -> 2 seats, cloned phi=1 -> 1 seat.

Two runs of the SAME scripted vendor measure the noise floor phi=0.780661975551146. Independent cross-vendor phi sits below that floor; cloned cross-vendor phi sits at the floor. A correlator that always reports 2 seats is rejected against the cloned pair.
Token spend on this G-1 arm is 0. Live paid calls to both vendors were not executed. Keys were inspected for presence only and never printed.

implementation.mechanism: Identical prompt bytes and identical canonical-token scoring. Joint 2x2 error table (both right, both wrong, each alone wrong). Pearson/phi on the error indicators. Effective seats n_eff = 2 / (1 + rho). Scripted personas plant independent vs shared failure modes. Same-vendor two-run rho is the noise floor. A nameplate correlator that always returns 2 is rejected.

negative_controls.description: always_two_seats ignores the joint table and reports effective_seats=2 on a cloned shared-failure pair whose honest n_eff is near 1.
Appending a vendor-specific suffix to one prompt must make prompt_parity.ok false while scoring remains the same function.

question: On a question set with known answers, when Claude is wrong how often is Codex wrong on the SAME item, and what is the effective number of independent seats rather than the nominal count of two vendor names?
question_answer: On the scripted 120-item scored set the harness discriminates. Independent personas: phi=0.0122, P(codex wrong | claude wrong)=0.1923, effective seats=1.9759 of 2 nominal. Cloned shared-failure personas: phi=0.7987, P(codex wrong | claude wrong)=0.9231, effective seats=1.1119 — expensive duplication, not a second seat. Same-vendor two-run floor phi=0.7807. Live paid Claude+Codex arm was NOT run (owner-gated; token spend 0). SUCCESS:TST-0292
question_or_target: model-diverse and vendor-diverse selection buys nothing if the models share failure modes. Measure conditional error correlation and report effective seats. Requires live paid API calls to both vendors, so it is serialized and gated.
residual_unknowns: Live paid Claude vs Codex correlation on a natural question set is unmeasured. The numbers in this receipt are for scripted personas with planted failure modes, which prove the harness distinguishes real diversity from duplication. They are not a claim about Anthropic or OpenAI production models.

A live Codex human pass is not claimed.

tests.name: Conditional error correlation over at least 100 scored items per vendor, with joint table and effective seats
Prompt-parity: identical prompts and identical scoring
Same-vendor baseline: two runs of the same model as the noise floor any cross-vendor correlation is compared against
Negative control: a nameplate correlator that always returns 2 seats must be rejected on the cloned pair

title: Are the vendor-diverse seats actually independent, or do they fail together
